question: In the light of the rapid and alarming deterioration of the human rights situation in Togo, where 35 political prisoners entered a hunger strike to denounce their prolonged arbitrary detention, lack of fair-trial guarantees, intimidation, and ill-treatment, what concrete actions will the Vice President/High Representative undertake to address the immediate risks to their lives and the broader pattern of human rights violations?

The detainees, journalists, academics, human rights defenders, activists, and students, are held solely for exercising fundamental freedoms, and the status of their health has now reached a critical stage. 1.

Considering Parliament’s resolution of 11 September 20251, and the fact that Togo remains bound by the Economic Community of West African States court judgments on arbitrary detention, the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, and the Opinions of the United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention, how does the Vice President/High Representative intend to promote the effective implementation of these legally and politically binding instruments?

Furthermore, what specific steps will the Vice President/High Representative take to publicly address these violations, to mobilise coordinated action with the European External Action Service, the United Nations, the African Union and regional bodies, and to support the creation of a European mechanism capable of monitoring and responding to the ongoing repression in Togo?
Texts adopted, P10_TA(2025)0194.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.5.2026) The EU is pleased to report recent positive progress regarding the situation of some prisoners in Togo. As part of a Presidential pardon in January 2026, more than 1 500 prisoners were released, including an Irish-Togolese citizen, who was the subject of an European Parliament urgency debate leading to the above-mentioned resolution of 11 September 2025.

The EU has been following closely the situation and has made continuous diplomatic efforts in Brussels and in Lomé to ensure full respect of human rights, right to due process, and better prison conditions.

The EU Delegation in Lomé, Member States’ embassies and the UN system will continue to work together to pursue dialogue conducive to strengthening human rights and democracy with both the Togolese authorities and other stakeholders through political dialogue and specific human rights actions.
